title.narrative: Enhancing Inclusive WASH Services for Vulnerable Communities and IDPs in Buale, Middle Juba, Jubaland State, Somalia

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia continues to face compounded effects from the 2020–2023 drought, severe floods in late 2023 and mid-2024, and the looming threat of another multi-season drought. These recurring climate shocks have overwhelmed coping capacities and deepened vulnerability, particularly in southern areas like Buale district in Middle Juba. In recent months, flooding and drought have displaced thousands, damaged livelihoods, and severely disrupted access to basic services. Forecasts for the upcoming Hagaa season (June–August 2025) predict above-normal rainfall, increasing risks to public health and WASH systems in the area.ltbrgtThis project, implemented by Lifeline Gedo (LLG), aims to improve inclusive and equitable access to lifesaving Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services for displaced and vulnerable communities in Buale. These populations face overlapping crises including displacement, food insecurity, disease outbreaks, and disrupted services. Current estimates indicate increasing displacement due to drought and floods, while WASH needs remain critical due to lack of safe water, inadequate sanitation, contamination of water sources, and limited hygiene awareness—factors that exacerbate malnutrition and waterborne diseases.ltbrgtAlthough humanitarian efforts have been reprioritized due to funding constraints, Buale remains a priority district under the 2025 Humanitarian Needs Response Plan (HNRP) and is classified as IPC Phase 4, reflecting severe food insecurity and acute malnutrition. Closure of health and nutrition facilities has reduced access to essential care, underscoring the need for preventive WASH interventions to curb disease and protect vulnerable groups.ltbrgtThe project will prioritize displaced households, minority and marginalized groups, persons with disabilities (PWDs), older persons, and female-headed households. It adopts gender-sensitive and inclusive approaches to ensure meaningful participation of women and persons with specific needs. Protection mainstreaming will address barriers to access, risks of exploitation, and harmful coping mechanisms such as child marriage and gender-based violence during water collection.ltbrgtKey interventions by LLG include:ltbrgt-Rehabilitation, protection, and equipping of strategic water sources (pumps, elevated tanks, distribution networks) serving rural communities, schools, health and nutrition centers, and IDPs.ltbrgt-Extension and improvement of existing water supply systems including piping, pumping, water tanks, and kiosks.ltbrgt-Construction of new emergency latrines, including PWD-friendly facilities, with handwashing stations for vulnerable IDPs and host communities.ltbrgt-Distribution of hygiene kits and sanitation tools to enhance solid waste management at the community level.ltbrgt-Hygiene promotion campaigns delivered through trained community promoters via mass outreach, house-to-house visits, and radio messaging.ltbrgtThis project aligns with the 2025 HNRP priorities in WASH, Health, Nutrition, and Food Security, and coordinates closely with the Protection Cluster and relevant Areas of Responsibility (AoRs) to ensure access to specialized services including GBV and child protection case management.ltbrgtBy enhancing inclusive WASH access and integrating protection principles, Lifeline Gedo (LLG) aims to reduce preventable diseases, restore dignity, and strengthen resilience among vulnerable populations in Buale. This intervention is crucial to safeguarding lives and rebuilding community coping mechanisms in one of Somalia’s most affected districts.ltbrgtlt/pgt
